title: Grateful Dead Live at Portland Memorial Coliseum on 1973-06-24
lineage: set 1: SBD> ?>C> CD> EAC> SHN; set 2: SBD> MR> C> D> CD> EAC> SHN

ai_review.summary: High‑quality soundboard capture of a stellar Dark Star > Eyes > China Doll medley, even though the first set is incomplete.
ai_review.review: The show shines thanks to an extended, soaring Dark Star that seamlessly flows into a high‑energy Eyes and a haunting China Doll – a pairing many fans rank among the best of ’73.  The Cotsman soundboard tape is clear and balances the dual‑guitar interplay beautifully, though the first set is missing several songs, leaving the archival record incomplete.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the performance 4–5 stars and praise the Dark Star medley; recording quality is consistently described as good to excellent, yielding an overall strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, well‑balanced tape that captures the dual‑guitar interplay; however the archive is missing a large portion of the first set and some minor lyrical flubs are noted.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is incomplete in this release; second set features a seamless Dark Star > Eyes > China Doll medley with high energy and tight transitions.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for soaring guitar work, quick jam sections, vocal delivery in Dark Star, and standout interplay with Bob.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for percolating bass rhythms, a memorable ‘Philo‑stop’ vibe, and strong groove that drives the jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Recognized for juicy phased effects on rhythm guitar and solid vocal contributions; overall not bad.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux adds tasteful touches near the end of the Dark Star jam, enhancing the texture without overpowering.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann described as a genius with brilliant drumming that underpins the improvisations.
